previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a morbidly obese male with HLA-B27 positive ankylosing spondylitis, hypertension, asthma, obstructive sleep apnea, and anxiety, was admitted for acute-on-chronic bilateral sacroiliac joint pain, worse on the left. He reported poor rehabilitation experience after a prior admission and worsening pain at home. Labs showed elevated inflammatory markers without signs of infection. Pain was managed with a return to Dilaudid, acetaminophen, ibuprofen, and cyclobenzaprine. Prednisone 20 mg daily was started as a bridge to biologic therapy. Rheumatology recommended outpatient initiation of anti-TNF inhibitors pending infectious disease clearance and Quantiferon Gold testing. The patient improved clinically, was discharged home with home health services, and given a plan for follow-up and medication tapering.
problems: Ankylosing spondylitis sacral and sacrococcygeal region

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ w/ PMH of ankylosing spondylitis (HLAB27 
positive, tried sulfasalazine, etanercept, adalimumab, 
infliximab, golimumab), recently admitted for pain control, 
discharged on oral steroids with plan for outpatient initiation 
of TNF-alpha inhibitors, presents with bilateral hip/sacroiliac 
joint pain for pain control. 

#Ankylosing Spondylitis/Bilateral SI joint pain: He presented 
with worsening bilateral hip pain over the past 1.5 weeks. On 
admission, CRP 2.7 and ESR 42, both lower than prior levels.  
Given that CRP elevations do not necessarily correlate with SI 
inflammation, this episode of pain is likely secondary to 
ankylosing spondylitis flare. Rheumatology was consulted with 
recs for steroid injections in bilateral sacroiliac joints and 
avoiding systemic steroid therapy, as it is not supported by the 
literature. Interventional Radiology completed bilateral CT 
guided SI joint injections ___. He had improved pain with 
reduced IV dilaudid use, weaned to only PO dilaudid on 
discharge. He has been hesitant to try anti-TNF alpha agents due 
to prior infections. Hep B and C screens were negative on prior 
admission. Quantiferon TB-Gold was negative with unlikely M. 
tuberculosis complex infection. Plan is to start TNF alpha 
inhibitors with Rheumatologist Dr. ___ ___. He will continue 
prednisone 40 mg daily, start taper once he starts TNF alpha 
inhibitor therapy.

#Hypertension: SBPs 140s-150s, likely exacerbated by pain and 
chronic steroid use. We increased home lisinopril to 20 mg 
daily. 

#Asthma: he was put on ipratropium bromide, albuterol inhaler, 
monteleukast and fluticasone inhaler. 

#Anxiety: continue home sertraline.

EXAMINATION:  CT-guided bilateral injections.

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with HLA + ankylosing spondylitis presenting with
acute on chronic hip and bilateral SI joint pain. Please perform steroid
injection in b/l sacroiliac joints. Please ___ for any clarification.  //
Long acting steroid injection in SI joints for acute pain exacerbation.
?Inflammation in bilateral SI joints

PHYSICIANS:  Dr. ___, (radiology fellow) and Dr. ___, radiology
attending, who was present for key points and supervised the procedure.

MEDICATION:  None.

COMPARISON:  Bilateral sacroiliac joint radiographs attempted ___.

PROCEDURE DETAILS:  Following discussion of the risks, benefits and
alternatives to the procedure, informed written patient consent was obtained. 
The patient was brought to the CT suite and placed prone on the table. An
initial limited noncontrast CT was performed to mark the sites, please see
below for details.

A preprocedure time-out was performed using 3 patient identifiers. The skin
was prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.

Right sacroiliac joint:  Approximately 2cc of 1% lidocaine was infiltrated
into the skin and subcutaneous tissues for local anesthesia. Using
intermittent CT fluoroscopic guidance, a 19 gauge 17 cm needle was advanced
into the right sacroiliac joint.  Upon confirmation of needle position, a 2 cc
solution of 0.25% bupivacaine and 40 mg Kenalog was injected.  The needle was
removed and manual compression was applied achieve hemostasis.

Left sacroiliac joint: Approximately 2cc of 1% lidocaine was infiltrated into
the skin and subcutaneous tissues for local anesthesia. Using intermittent CT
fluoroscopic guidance, a new 19 gauge 17 cm needle was advanced into the right
sacroiliac joint. Upon confirmation of needle position, a 2 cc solution of
0.25% bupivacaine and 40 mg Kenalog was injected.   The needle was removed and
manual compression was applied achieve hemostasis.

 There were no immediate post-procedure complications and the patient left the
department in stable condition.

The patient reported no change in pain symptoms immediately following
injections.

FINDINGS: 

Mild narrowing and subchondral sclerosis of bilateral sacroiliac joints.

IMPRESSION:


1. Mild narrowing and subchondral sclerosis of bilateral sacroiliac joints.
2. Technically successful CT guided bilateral sacroiliac joint steroid
injections.
